title: World hills and climbable mounds — strict wave-two research dossier

method.inclusion: Named hill, summit, mound or defining upper objective reached by a meaningful legal public walk on ordinary non-technical terrain.
method.source_gate: At least two useful sources per retained row, including an official, land-manager, municipal, heritage or other first-party source; discovery sources never establish access alone.
method.confidence_gate: Every value in confidence must be high.
method.dedupe_gate: IDs, normalized names, aliases and external IDs checked globally; every candidate checked against all catalogue coordinates and internally at <=120 m.
method.hard_exclusions: No scrambling, chains, ladders, exposed ridges, tidal or seasonal route judgement, technical mountain terrain, private summits, filler or generic drive-up lookouts.

included.s: A paved desert ascent to the public overlook below a protected research summit.
included.q: Tumamoc Hill Summit Overlook Tucson United States
included.w: Walk 1.5 miles up a paved research road through a desert laboratory founded in 1903. The public route gains about 700 feet and ends at the cable-marked summit overlook; the ecological reserve beyond the cable is restricted.

facts.claim: The public is encouraged to walk the paved hill road daily from 04:00 to 22:00; the ascent is 1.5 miles and gains about 700 feet.
Walkers must remain on the paved road and inside cable-marked overlooks; the research area beyond the cable is not public.
The Desert Laboratory was founded in 1903 and includes continuously monitored ecological plots dating from 1906.

sources.role: current public route, hours and restrictions

sources.publisher: University of Arizona College of Science

public_access_evidence.summary: Daily 04:00–22:00 on the paved road to cable-marked overlooks; do not cross the cable into the research reserve.

ordinary_walk_evidence.summary: Paved 1.5-mile ascent with benches and switchbacks; no technical terrain.

coordinate_basis.summary: Mapped public viewpoint at the summit cable boundary, not the restricted peak 68 metres west.

included.accidental_discovery_rationale: A neighbourhood fitness climb unexpectedly becomes a century-long desert science story.

included.s: Climb America's pioneering landfill mountain on a city park trail.
included.q: Mount Trashmore Virginia Beach United States
included.w: Virginia Beach turned 640,000 tons of compacted waste into a 60-foot grass mountain. Follow the 1.3-mile Mountain Trail over one of the United States' earliest landfill-to-park transformations.

facts.claim: The main mound is 60 feet high and 800 feet long and was formed from 640,000 tons of compacted waste and clean soil.
The public Mountain Trail is a 1.3-mile park route over the mound.

sources.publisher: City of Virginia Beach Parks & Recreation
sources.role: identity, construction, dimensions and current park status
current Mountain Trail and visitor access

public_access_evidence.summary: Open municipal park; current works affect listed facilities rather than the named Mountain Trail.

ordinary_walk_evidence.summary: A maintained 1.3-mile city-park trail climbs the grass mound.

coordinate_basis.summary: Mapped summit point within the official mound footprint.

included.accidental_discovery_rationale: What looks like a suburban green hill is municipal waste transformed into a landmark.

included.s: A car-free paved climb to a civic summit of bridges, monuments and Easter history.
included.q: Mount Rubidoux Riverside California United States
included.w: Paved roads and dirt trails spiral through a 161-acre landmark park to the summit. The city keeps vehicles out, leaving a 45-to-60-minute climb tied to Riverside's long-running outdoor Easter sunrise service.

facts.claim: The 161-acre city park has 3.5 miles of paved roads and dirt trails, is closed to vehicles and takes roughly 45–60 minutes to walk.
The summit is associated with Riverside's historic outdoor non-denominational Easter sunrise service.

sources.publisher: City of Riverside Parks, Recreation and Community Services
sources.role: current access, route, park facts and history

public_access_evidence.summary: Municipal landmark park open dawn to dusk; pedestrian access only on the summit roads and trails.

ordinary_walk_evidence.summary: Paved road and dirt-trail options form a non-technical 45–60 minute climb.

coordinate_basis.summary: Mapped summit point cross-checked to the official park objective.

included.accidental_discovery_rationale: A local exercise loop reveals itself as a car-free civic pilgrimage summit.

included.s: Climb A Mountain past hundreds of Hohokam petroglyphs.
included.q: Hayden Butte A Mountain Tempe Arizona United States
included.w: The Leonard Monti Trail climbs a small Sonoran butte whose slopes preserve roughly 500 Hohokam petroglyphs. At the top, Tempe's giant steel-and-concrete A sits inside a landscape sacred to four Southern Tribes.

facts.claim: The preserve contains approximately 500 Hohokam petroglyphs dating from about AD 750–1450 and is sacred to four Southern Tribes.
The 60-foot summit A is steel and concrete, and visitors must stay on the designated Leonard Monti Trail.

sources.role: Indigenous history, petroglyphs and summit A

ordinary_walk_evidence.summary: The named municipal trail is a short pedestrian summit ascent without technical obstacles.

coordinate_basis.summary: Summit point for the named butte, checked against the official trail objective.

included.accidental_discovery_rationale: A familiar college-town letter marks a much older, sacred petroglyph landscape.

included.a: Pilot Butte State Scenic Viewpoint, Bend
included.s: Walk from Bend's streets to the top of an extinct cinder cone.
included.q: Pilot Butte Bend Oregon United States
included.w: Three trails leave Bend's east-side streets for the summit of a cinder cone about 188,000 years old. The year-round base path gains roughly 480 feet; only the separate summit driving road is seasonal.

facts.claim: All three official trails reach the summit, and the east base parking and pedestrian approach remain available year-round.
The cinder cone is about 188,000 years old and the walking ascent gains about 480 feet.

included.s: Climb Boston's last surviving summit from the night that forced an evacuation.

facts.claim: Continental troops fortified the height overnight in March 1776, contributing to the British evacuation of Boston.
The grounds are free and open daily, with wide paved paths, stairs and ramps climbing the hill.

included.accidental_discovery_rationale: A modest neighbourhood hill explains a decisive overnight change in Boston's siege.

included.s: Climb a precisely sculpted waste mountain inside Isamu Noguchi's park.
included.q: Mount Moere Moerenuma Park Sapporo Japan
included.w: Five routes, including a straight stair, climb a 62.4-metre artificial mountain shaped from non-combustible waste and construction spoil. Its exact 2,004-centimetre summit width nods to Isamu Noguchi's centenary year.

facts.claim: The artificial mountain was made with non-combustible waste and construction spoil, rises 62.4 metres above sea level and has five ascent routes.
The 2,004-centimetre summit width marks 2004, the centenary of Isamu Noguchi's birth, within a park designed as one sculpture.

coordinate_basis.summary: Mapped centre of the flat summit objective.

facts.claim: Seoul's official route runs from Eungbong Station to the Palgakjeong pavilion on the 81-metre mountain.
The slope is especially associated with forsythia that blooms early in Seoul and views of the Han River bridges.

included.w: Public roads and walking routes climb a wildlife reserve inside Bloemfontein. The hill remembers British naval guns placed here during the South African War; walkers share the landscape with game and are advised to go in groups by day.

Mangaung's 2026 work programme includes visitor information boards for Franklin Nature Reserve and Naval Hill.
